title: Dashboard schedule mirror parity for the SPY refresh ladder
times_source: read from the scheduled_job decorators in run_scheduler.py, not assumed

what_the_gap_had_cost.event: on 2026-08-27 all three rungs of the evening ladder FAILED; the 00:45 last look on 2026-08-28 completed and brought the series up to date

defects_visible.what: SPY_REFRESH_PM_R1 and _R2 reported lifecycle_status recovered, recovered_at 2026-08-27T22:20:14Z
defects_visible.mechanism: later_same_stream matches on job_type and both sat in the `other` catch-all; a catch-all is not a stream

defects_visible.what: the retries read 'The job emitted an unclassified error ... reconcile current broker state' - broker advice for a data job that never touches the broker
none of the three had a schedule-panel row, so neither the failures nor the recovery could be reported

stream_design.three_rungs_share_one_type: so later_same_stream expresses the ladder: a missed rung caught by a later rung is a recovery, through the mechanism that already existed for stop-repair
stream_design.last_look_is_its_own_type: it asks for the PREVIOUS TRADING DAY, not today's close; folding it in would let a 00:45 success mark an evening rung recovered for a question that rung never asked

language.caught_by_a_later_rung: This rung of the post-close SPY ladder did not run; the series was brought up to date when <job> completed. No immediate action.
language.not_caught: unchanged severe wording - the series is a day short and tomorrow's Track 1 slots meet a freshness refusal
language.why_conditional: Stage 5ZZC found that two retries reporting failure on every good day is an alarm people learn to ignore; copying the 16:20 wording onto the rungs would rebuild that alarm via the missed path. Making it unconditional would be the opposite error - a total ladder failure reading mild. Both directions are pinned by tests.
language.last_look: states its own consequence including the Monday case: the evening ladder last ran thirty-one hours earlier

the_check_parity_cannot_make.problem: parity compares slot IDS only; a row at the wrong minute passes it and then reports overdue every day forever
the_check_parity_cannot_make.method: derives the schedule from run_scheduler.py decorators via AST and compares clocks in both directions
the_check_parity_cannot_make.proof: mutation M3 moves SPY_REFRESH_PM_R1 one hour early - parity still passes, only this test catches it

attribution.method: reverted both production edits, re-ran the same suites, diffed the failure sets

pre_existing_failures: test_flag_on_adds_a_window_band_per_sleeve - expects a Calm one-shot band from before Calm became two phases
test_state_slot_count_is_seventy_in_track1_only - pins the old 70-slot literal, the table holds 71

no_phantom_alarm.note: the 00:45 job ran today and is recognised; this was the risk Stage 5ZZS declined to take without measuring first

gate_and_slot_invariants.gates_reached_only_via: the existing SPY coverage and verification records

safety_after.run_scheduler_py: read only, never written - not even by the mutation harness

backend_restart_required.reason: Python imports a module once per process, so the running backend holds the pre-5ZZT versions
backend_restart_required.scheduler_impact: none - a backend-only restart does not disturb the scheduler (Stage 5ZZO)

still_open.what: the `other` bucket is still a shared stream
still_open.detail: TRACK1_STOP_REPAIR_* and TRACK1_AUDIT_* are deliberately kept from the legacy prefixes and were never given types of their own, so they sit in `other` together. All completed today, so nothing receives a false recovery now; the next failed Track 1 stop-repair will be closed by an unrelated audit job completing afterwards.
still_open.disposition: same defect, different jobs - wants its own stage

still_open.detail: the 00:45 job on the 28th genuinely repaired the 27th failure, but the journal reads one day at a time, so the 27th still shows three open failures with no sign of what fixed them

still_open.what: five pre-existing failures listed above, none of them this stage's
